title: A compass is not a map: why startup rules and frameworks can't predict success
summary: Jason Cohen argues there is no map to startup success. Every piece of advice has successes and failures on both sides, and successful startups are by definition outliers that statistics can't predict. Treat frameworks and famous origin stories as a candy store for inspiration, not laws, and find your own way.

principles.text: Startup advice is a compass, not a map: it shows a direction, not whether you should go that way.
principles.quote: A compass tells you **which way is north, not whether you should be heading north**.

principles.text: For any piece of startup advice, both followers and opposites have succeeded and failed, so the advice alone proves little.
principles.quote: for every piece of advice `P`, there are many successes and failures of startups who did `P`, and also many successes and failures of startups that did the opposite of `P`.

principles.text: Successful startups are anomalies, and trends can't predict outliers.
principles.quote: by definition the successful ones are anomalies**. Statistics show trends, but **trends don't predict outliers**.

principles.text: A successful startup looks like an unsuccessful one at the start, so nothing reliably predicts the outlier.
Don't treat frameworks, dogma or favorite-startup origin stories as laws; mine them for sparks and pick what fits you.
principles.quote: Don't confuse startup frameworks or dogma or the origin story of your favorite startup with laws.

principles.text: Use advice like a candy store: choose what suits who you already are, then keep moving.
principles.quote: There's no map. That's OK. Keep moving.
